hook: EMIs ran for a phone that never came; retailer told to pay *₹1.14 lakh*
hook_b: EMIs ran for a phone that never came; retailer told to pay *₹1.14 lakh*
tldr: A Hyderabad district consumer commission ordered an electronics retailer to refund ₹74,698 and pay ₹40,000 more after a buyer's zero-interest EMIs began without the phone ever being delivered.

beats.what: The commission ordered a ₹74,698 refund, ₹30,000 for mental agony and ₹10,000 litigation costs, and told the retailer to get the loan account closed.
beats.why: The buyer shared an OTP in the store in March 2024 to process a zero-interest EMI purchase; the first ₹4,204 EMI was deducted on April 3, 2024, with no phone handed over.
beats.care: Store EMI deals often need an OTP at the counter; the commission's order turned on who could prove delivery.

causes.label: OTP shared for EMI, no phone

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The retailer said the buyer got the phone and alleged a wider loan-resale scheme; the commission found no FIR or chargesheet backing that.
